NASA article id: 19740033277
Title: New two-metric theory of gravity with prior geometry
Abstract: A Lagrangian-based metric theory of gravity is developed with three adjustable constants and two tensor fields, one of which is a nondynamic 'flat space metric' eta. With a suitable cosmological model and a particular choice of the constants, the 'post-Newtonian limit' of the theory agrees, in the current epoch, with that of general relativity theory (GRT); consequently the theory is consistent with current gravitation experiments. Because of the role of eta, the gravitational 'constant' G is time-dependent and gravitational waves travel null geodesics of eta rather than the physical metric g. Gravitational waves possess six degrees of freedom. The general exact static spherically-symmetric solution is a four-parameter family. Future experimental tests of the theory are discussed.
Authors: Lightman, A. P., Lee, D. L.

modes.answer_text: The NASA article titled "New two-metric theory of gravity with prior geometry" by A. P. Lightman and D. L. Lee, published in Physical Review D - Particles and Fields on November 15, 1973, discusses a Lagrangian-based metric theory of gravity that includes three adjustable constants and one tensor field. The study shows that the 'post-Newtonian limit' of this theory aligns with general relativity theory (GRT) in the current epoch. This consistency is due to the inclusion of a nondynamic 'flat space metric' eta, which alters the gravitational constant G to be time-dependent and influences the propagation of gravitational waves through null geodesics of eta rather than the physical metric g. The study also discusses future experimental tests of this theory.

Using NASA article metadata, a concise factual summary is as follows: This paper presents a Lagrangian-based metric theory of gravity with three adjustable constants and two tensor fields. One of these tensor fields is a nondynamic 'flat space metric' eta. The theory agrees with the current epoch of general relativity (GRT) in terms of the 'post-Newtonian limit'. Gravitational waves possess six degrees of freedom, and they travel null geodesics of the adjustable constant eta rather than the physical metric g. Future experimental tests are discussed. This work was first published by A. P. Lightman and D. L. Lee in November 1973 under the title "New two-metric theory of gravity with prior geometry".
